# SmoothNumbers — numbers built only from the wheels

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** planned: new, not yet proved · **Diagram:** [Survivor shares and analytic inputs](../../GRAPH.md#survivor-shares-and-analytic-inputs)

The numbers up to x whose prime factors are all wheels up to y. Rankin's bound: their count is at most x to a power alpha times the product over the wheels of one over one minus the wheel to the minus alpha, for any alpha between 0 and 1; at alpha = 1 that product is the reciprocal of the survivor share. A lower bound counts the products of the wheels directly, and a Buchstab-type identity removes the largest wheel. Ford Chapter 5.

## Planned

**Plan:** rankin_upper: each counted number n has (x/n)^alpha >= 1; sum over all products of the wheels (a finite Euler product). smooth_count_lower: products of at most floor(log x / log y) wheels with repetition are distinct and at most x. smooth_buchstab: sort by largest prime factor.

**Scope:** Tier 1: all three are finite.
